key_claims: Tribal loyalties are strongest among the Pushtuns of eastern and southern Afghanistan; organized action by an entire tribe is rare.
The Afghan insurgency is strongest among traditionalist groups such as the Pushtuns of Paktia and the Nuristanis and Tajiks near the Pakistani border.
Tribes resist the Marxist government and the Soviets mainly to preserve traditional ways, not out of anti-communist ideology.
The Soviets can offer weapons and money and threaten retaliation, but tribal allies are unreliable and would turn on them when advantageous.
Tribes in northern Pakistan are probably too small and isolated to be a useful Soviet target.
Many Iranian border tribes probably assist Afghan insurgents, partly for smuggling income.
